title: Present Simple vs Present Continuous
rule_en: Use the present simple for routines, facts, and things that are generally true: "I work in finance." Use the present continuous for something happening right now, or a temporary situation around now: "I'm working from home this week."
rule_bg: Сегашно просто за рутина, факти и трайни неща: „I work in finance.“ Сегашно продължително за нещо, което се случва точно сега или временно, около момента на говорене: „I'm working from home this week.“

examples.en: She usually checks her email at 8. Right now she's checking a report instead.
examples.bg: Обикновено проверява имейла в 8. В момента проверява доклад вместо това.

examples.en: We meet every Monday. This Monday we're meeting online because of the storm.
examples.bg: Срещаме се всеки понеделник. Този понеделник се срещаме онлайн заради бурята.

examples.en: I don't usually drink coffee, but I'm drinking one now, it's been a long day.
examples.bg: Обикновено не пия кафе, но сега пия, беше дълъг ден.

exercises.sentence: Normally I ___ at 9, but today I'm starting at 7.
Listen! Someone ___ at the door.
Water ___ at 100 degrees Celsius.
I can't talk now, I ___ a client.
He ___ three languages: Bulgarian, English and German.

title: Present Perfect vs Past Simple
rule_en: Use the present perfect when the time isn't finished, or the exact time doesn't matter: "I've sent the invoice." (it's done, no date given). Use the past simple when the time is specific and finished: "I sent the invoice yesterday."
rule_bg: Сегашно перфектно, когато моментът не е приключил или точното време не е важно: „I've sent the invoice.“ Минало просто, когато времето е конкретно и приключило: „I sent the invoice yesterday.“

examples.en: I've worked here for six years. I started in 2020.
examples.bg: Работя тук от 6 години. Започнах през 2020.

examples.en: Have you finished the report? — Yes, I finished it this morning.
examples.bg: Приключи ли доклада? — Да, приключих го тази сутрин.

examples.en: We've never been to that supplier's factory.
examples.bg: Никога не сме били на фабриката на този доставчик.

exercises.sentence: I ___ this company since 2019.
She ___ the meeting last Tuesday.
___ you ever ___ to Berlin?
He ___ the proposal yesterday afternoon.
We ___ already ___ three suppliers this month.

title: Present Perfect with FOR and SINCE
rule_en: Use FOR with a length of time: for five years, for two weeks, for a month. Use SINCE with a starting point: since 2020, since Monday, since I joined.
rule_bg: FOR с продължителност: for five years, for two weeks. SINCE с начална точка: since 2020, since Monday, since I joined.

examples.en: I've known her for ten years.
The price hasn't changed since January.
examples.bg: Цената не се е променила от януари.

examples.en: They've used this supplier since they opened the business.
examples.bg: Ползват този доставчик, откакто отвориха бизнеса.

exercises.sentence: I've lived in Plovdiv ___ 2015.
We haven't spoken ___ three months.
She's been the manager ___ the company started.
He's been on sick leave ___ a week.
The invoice has been overdue ___ last Friday.

title: Past Simple vs Past Continuous
rule_en: Use the past continuous for an action in progress at a point in the past, often interrupted by a shorter action in the past simple: "I was writing the report when the client called."
rule_bg: Минало продължително за действие, което е било в ход в определен момент в миналото, често прекъснато от по-кратко действие в минало просто: „I was writing the report when the client called.“

examples.en: While she was presenting, the projector stopped working.
examples.bg: Докато представяше, проекторът спря да работи.

examples.en: I was checking my email when I saw the news.
examples.bg: Проверявах имейла си, когато видях новината.

examples.en: They were negotiating for hours before they agreed.
examples.bg: Преговаряха с часове, преди да се съгласят.

exercises.sentence: I ___ lunch when my phone rang.

The meeting ___ at nine and finished at ten.
She ___ to the client when her laptop crashed.
He ___ the office at exactly 6 pm yesterday.

title: Future: WILL, GOING TO, Present Continuous
rule_en: Use WILL for decisions made now and predictions: "I'll call him." Use GOING TO for plans already decided: "We're going to launch in March." Use the present continuous for fixed arrangements with a time and place: "I'm meeting the client at 3."
rule_bg: WILL за решения, взети в момента, и предвиждания: „I'll call him.“ GOING TO за вече решени планове: „We're going to launch in March.“ Сегашно продължително за уговорени срещи с точно време и място: „I'm meeting the client at 3.“

examples.en: I think prices will rise next year.
examples.bg: Мисля, че цените ще се вдигнат догодина.

examples.en: We're going to open a second office, it's already decided.
examples.bg: Ще отворим втори офис, вече е решено.

examples.en: I'm flying to London on Friday, the ticket is booked.
examples.bg: Летя до Лондон в петък, билетът е купен.

title: First Conditional (real future situations)
rule_en: Use the first conditional for real, possible future situations: IF + present simple, ... WILL + base verb. "If the client agrees, we'll sign tomorrow." Never use WILL after IF.
rule_bg: Първи тип условно изречение за реални, възможни бъдещи ситуации: IF + сегашно просто, ... WILL + основна форма. „If the client agrees, we'll sign tomorrow.“ Никога не се слага WILL след IF.

examples.en: If we cut the price, they'll order more.
examples.bg: Ако намалим цената, ще поръчат повече.

examples.en: If it rains tomorrow, we'll move the event indoors.
examples.bg: Ако вали утре, ще преместим събитието на закрито.

examples.en: She'll be upset if you cancel again.
examples.bg: Ще се разстрои, ако отмениш пак.

exercises.sentence: If we ___ the deadline, the client will be angry.
